To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the principal component analysis of gravitational wave burst waveforms from rotating stellar core collapse can be used to extract information about the physical parameters associated to the collapse.

the principal component analysis method provides a means to reconstruct the gravitational wave signals associated with core collapse, and the reconstructed signal may provide useful information on the physical properties of the progenitor star.

(1) The reconstructed signal and the eigenvector amplitude posterior distributions are consistent with the original signal, (2) the posterior distribution of the pulse arrival time is consistent with the original simulation time of the signal, (3) the posterior distribution for the amplitude of the first eigenvector provides information on the mass and rotation of the progenitor, and (4) the amplitude of the second eigenvector posterior distribution provides information on the nuclear equation of State.

the extraction of the physical parameters of the progenitor star and the equation of state of the core from the observation of a gravitational wave signal from a rotating stellar core.

the principal component analysis and Bayesian techniques are useful tools for extracting the physical properties of core collapse events from the associated gravitational wave signals.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the gravitational wave signal associated with a stellar core collapse event is a complex waveform, and that the principal component analysis approach provides a powerful method to extract physical information from the waveform.
the principal component analysis technique is a useful tool to reconstruct the gravitational wave signal from a rotating core collapse, and to estimate its physical parameters.
the information provided by the eigenvector amplitude posterior probability distribution functions can be used to constrain the physical parameters associated to the core collapse and bounce event.
